Indianapolis

the Speedway, Mass Ave, the Cultural Trail & a deep immigrant table

Downtown & Wholesale District 37

Monument Circle, White River State Park, Indiana Ave

  1. Must see · Steakhouses & Fine Dining · Downtown & Wholesale District

    St. Elmo Steak House

    Order: The fiery shrimp cocktail (horseradish-loaded sauce, on the menu since 1947) and dry-aged USDA Prime steaks. Indianapolis' defining restaurant, in the Wholesale District since 1902 — bow-tied career servers, dark-panelled rooms, one of the city's great bourbon lists, and the only James Beard Award ever won in Indy (America's Classics, 2012). On Indianapolis Monthly's 2026 Best Restaurants.

    127 S Illinois St, Indianapolis, IN 46225

    Recommended by Wikipedia, Indianapolis Monthly, Axios Indianapolis, Tasting Table, Indy Today (6AM City)

  2. Must see · Delis, Sandwiches & Diners · Downtown & Wholesale District

    Shapiro's Delicatessen

    Order: Corned beef on house rye, the Reuben, potato latkes, matzo ball soup. Kosher-style deli-cafeteria opened as a grocery by Louis and Rebecca Shapiro in 1905, on South Meridian since 1912 — one of the few surviving Jewish delis in the Midwest. Order at the counter; carry your tray.

    808 S Meridian St, Indianapolis, IN 46225

    Recommended by Roadfood (Jane & Michael Stern), Nuvo, Indyencyclopedia, Visit Indy

  3. Must see · American & New American · Downtown & Wholesale District

    Harry & Izzy's

    Order: St. Elmo's shrimp cocktail (the fiery horseradish sauce) and steaks in a less formal room. St. Elmo's sister restaurant and next-door neighbour (1997) — an upscale American grill that shares St. Elmo's famous shrimp cocktail and steaks with a broader menu around a lively bar. On Indianapolis Monthly's Swoon List.

    Look for Wholesale District

    153 S Illinois St, Indianapolis, IN

    Recommended by Downtown Indy, Inc., Visit Indy, Indianapolis Monthly, WTHR 13

  4. Must see · Downtown & Wholesale District

    Soldiers' and Sailors' Monument

    The 284-ft neoclassical monument on Monument Circle, dedicated 1902 — the city's signature structure and literal centre of the original Mile Square plan. Free; observation deck and the Civil War museum below.

    Look for Monument Circle

    Monument Circle, Indianapolis, IN

    Recommended by Wikipedia, Indyencyclopedia, Arts Council of Indianapolis (Indy Arts Guide)

  5. Must see · Downtown & Wholesale District

    Indiana World War Memorial Plaza

    Five city blocks of memorials — the stepped-pyramid Indiana War Memorial (free military museum + Shrine Room), the Obelisk and the American Legion Mall. One of the largest memorial plazas in the US; free.

    Indiana World War Memorial Plaza (N Meridian St), Indianapolis, IN

    Recommended by Wikipedia, Visit Indy, The Cultural Landscape Foundation

  6. Must see · Downtown & Wholesale District

    White River State Park

    267-acre urban state park on both banks of the White River — the Central Canal walk, the zoo, Eiteljorg, Indiana State Museum, Victory Field and the old Washington Street bridge for walking.

    White River State Park, Indianapolis, IN

    Recommended by Wikipedia, The Cultural Landscape Foundation, Official Site

  7. Must see · Downtown & Wholesale District

    Scottish Rite Cathedral

    The 1929 Tudor-Gothic Masonic cathedral — the largest Scottish Rite building anywhere, with a 54-bell carillon tower; guided tours.

    650 N Meridian St, Indianapolis, IN 46204

    Recommended by Wikipedia, Indyencyclopedia, Saharchipedia

  8. Must see · Downtown & Wholesale District

    Madam Walker Legacy Center

    The 1927 Madam C.J. Walker Building (NHL) on historic Indiana Avenue — her company HQ and Art Deco theatre, the heart of Black Indianapolis jazz and culture; reopened 2020 after a $15M restoration.

    617 Indiana Ave, Indianapolis, IN

    Recommended by Wikipedia, Indiana Public Media, Wish-tv 8

  9. Must see · Downtown & Wholesale District

    Indianapolis Cultural Trail

    8-mile brick-and-stone bike/walk trail linking the downtown cultural districts with public art along the way — a $63M model for US urban trails. Pin marks a central point on the loop.

    Downtown loop (Alabama St / Mass Ave / Virginia Ave / Indiana Ave), Indianapolis, IN

    Recommended by Wikipedia, Indyencyclopedia, Indianapolis Business Journal

  10. Must see · Downtown & Wholesale District

    Crispus Attucks Museum

    Inside Crispus Attucks High School — Indiana's segregated Black high school, whose Oscar Robertson-led team won the 1955 state title — four galleries of African American history from the Underground Railroad to the Tuskegee Airmen.

    1140 Dr. Martin Luther King Jr. St, Indianapolis, IN

    Recommended by Wikipedia, Wish-tv 8, Visitindiana

  11. Must see · Breweries, Bars & Cocktails · Downtown & Wholesale District

    Slippery Noodle Inn

    Order: Live blues on two stages nightly, with bar food. Indiana's oldest continuously operating bar (1850, the Tremont House) — an Underground Railroad stop, Prohibition brewery and brothel before becoming the city's great blues bar; 1890 tin ceiling and century-old oak bar.

    372 S Meridian St, Indianapolis, IN

    Recommended by Wikipedia, Indyencyclopedia, Indianapolis Monthly

  12. Must see · Breweries, Bars & Cocktails · Downtown & Wholesale District

    Sun King Brewing

    Order: Sunlight Cream Ale and Osiris Pale Ale in the production-floor taproom. Indianapolis' largest brewery (2009) in the Cole-Noble district by Lockerbie — all-ages taproom with 25+ taps and tours.

    135 N College Ave, Indianapolis, IN

    Recommended by Wikipedia, Downtown Indy, Inc., Indianapolis Business Journal

  13. Must see · Mexican & Latin · Downtown & Wholesale District

    Julieta Taco Shop

    Order: Al pastor and carnitas on nixtamalized corn tortillas; the broccolini taco. Counter-service taqueria tucked into the Stutz building courtyard (Esteban Rosas & Gabriel Sañudo) — fresh masa tortillas, rotating tacos, lunch only. Named Indiana's best hole-in-the-wall taco joint (Cheapism) and on a national top-100 taco list.

    1060 N Capitol Ave, Suite 1-103 (Stutz courtyard), Indianapolis, IN

    Recommended by Indianapolis Monthly, FOX59, Cheapism (syndicated via Aol)

  14. Must see · Downtown & Wholesale District

    Indiana Statehouse

    The 1888 Renaissance Revival capitol with a stained-glass rotunda dome; free self-guided and guided tours on weekdays.

    200 W Washington St, Indianapolis, IN 46204

    Recommended by Wikipedia, Saharchipedia

  15. Must see · Downtown & Wholesale District

    Eiteljorg Museum

    Museum of American Indians and Western Art (1989) in White River State Park — Native contemporary art plus Western painting and sculpture.

    White River State Park, Indianapolis, IN

    Recommended by Wikipedia, Clio (Marshall University)

  16. Must see · Downtown & Wholesale District

    Indianapolis Zoo

    Zoo, aquarium and White River Gardens in White River State Park — dolphins, the Bicentennial orangutan centre, and the first triple-accredited zoo in the US.

    White River State Park, Indianapolis, IN

    Recommended by Wikipedia, Polis Center (Indiana University Indianapolis)

  17. Must see · Downtown & Wholesale District

    Lucas Oil Stadium

    Retractable-roof home of the Colts (2008) and of the NFL Combine, Final Fours and Big Ten title games.

    500 S Capitol Ave, Indianapolis, IN

    Recommended by Wikipedia, Structurae

  18. Must see · Steakhouses & Fine Dining · Downtown & Wholesale District

    Prime 47

    Order: Wet-aged prime filet with horseradish–bleu cheese crust; Cajun New York strip. Locally owned steakhouse in the Romanesque Revival Majestic Building, named for its street number — Indianapolis Monthly's 'Indy's Great Steakhouses' pick; WISH has called it Indy's No. 1 steakhouse.

    47 S Pennsylvania St (Majestic Building), Indianapolis, IN

    Recommended by Indianapolis Monthly, Wish-tv 8

  19. Worth the detour · American & New American · Downtown & Wholesale District

    Spoke & Steele

    Order: Dry-aged Duroc pork chop; the Spoke Burger; barrel-aged cocktails. Le Méridien's racing-themed, mid-century-modern restaurant and bar — Midwestern comfort food done ambitiously, with barrel-aged cocktails at a brass-edged bar.

    Look for Wholesale District

    123 S Illinois St (Le Méridien), Indianapolis, IN

    Recommended by Indianapolis Monthly, FOX59, Wish-tv 8, Edible Indy

  20. Worth the detour · Downtown & Wholesale District

    Indianapolis City Market

    Public market since 1821 in its 1886 D.A. Bohlen & Son hall (NRHP) — now a food hall; the catacombs of the old Tomlinson Hall lie underneath.

    222 E Market St, Indianapolis, IN

    Recommended by Wikipedia, Library of Congress (habs/Haer), Visitindiana

  21. Worth the detour · Downtown & Wholesale District

    Central Library

    Paul Cret's 1917 Beaux-Arts library on the War Memorial axis, joined to a six-storey glass atrium (2007); free, with the Vonnegut-era reading rooms.

    40 E St. Clair St, Indianapolis, IN

    Recommended by Wikipedia, Indianapolis Public Library, National Park SVC

  22. Worth the detour · Downtown & Wholesale District

    Christ Church Cathedral

    William Tinsley's 1857 English Gothic Revival church — the oldest building on Monument Circle.

    131 Monument Circle, Indianapolis, IN

    Recommended by Wikipedia, National Park SVC, Saharchipedia

  23. Worth the detour · Downtown & Wholesale District

    Victory Field

    The Indianapolis Indians' 1996 ballpark with its lawn seating and skyline view over the outfield — one of the best-loved minor-league parks in the US.

    White River State Park, Indianapolis, IN

    Recommended by Wikipedia, Visit Indy, Official Site

  24. Worth the detour · Downtown & Wholesale District

    Hilbert Circle Theatre

    A 1916 'deluxe movie palace' on Monument Circle, restored as home of the Indianapolis Symphony Orchestra (1,660 seats).

    Look for Monument Circle

    45 Monument Circle, Indianapolis, IN

    Recommended by Wikipedia, Official Site, Polis Center (Indiana University Indianapolis)

  25. Worth the detour · Downtown & Wholesale District

    Stutz Building

    The 1914 Stutz Motor Car factory (home of the Bearcat), five connected four-storey buildings now full of artist studios — the Stutz Artists Association's open-studio nights fill the halls.

    10th St & Capitol Ave, Indianapolis, IN

    Recommended by Indyencyclopedia, Saharchipedia, Indy Today (6AM City)

  26. Worth the detour · Downtown & Wholesale District

    NCAA Hall of Champions

    Michael Graves-designed NCAA headquarters and museum (2000) covering all 24 college sports, with a 1930s-style hardwood court upstairs.

    White River State Park, Indianapolis, IN

    Recommended by Wikipedia, Indyencyclopedia, Official Site

  27. Worth the detour · Breweries, Bars & Cocktails · Downtown & Wholesale District

    1933 Lounge by St. Elmo

    Order: St. Elmo shrimp cocktail and filet sliders with Prohibition-era cocktails. St. Elmo's upstairs lounge, named for the year Prohibition ended — brick walls, an 1898 back bar, the famous shrimp cocktail and filet sliders with classic cocktails. Indianapolis Monthly's No. 5 best bar.

    Look for Wholesale District

    127 S Illinois St (2nd floor of St. Elmo Steak House), Indianapolis, IN

    Recommended by Indianapolis Monthly, FOX59, Visit Indy

  28. Worth the detour · American & New American · Downtown & Wholesale District

    The Eagle's Nest

    Order: Steaks and seafood in Indiana's only revolving rooftop dining room. Rotating restaurant atop the 22-storey Hyatt Regency since 1977 — one of fewer than two dozen revolving rooftop restaurants left in North America; 360° views of downtown.

    Hyatt Regency Indianapolis (rooftop), 1 S Capitol Ave, Indianapolis, IN

    Recommended by Indianapolis Business Journal, Indianapolis Monthly, WRTV 6 (abc Indianapolis)

  29. Worth the detour · Pizza & Italian · Downtown & Wholesale District

    Nesso Italian Kitchen

    Order: Coastal Italian pastas (clams-and-broccolini linguine); regional Italian wine list. Coastal-Italian dining room in The Alexander hotel from Cunningham Restaurant Group — scratch pasta and one of Indiana's deepest Italian wine lists (Wine Spectator Award of Excellence 2025).

    Look for CityWay

    339 S Delaware St (The Alexander hotel), Indianapolis, IN

    Recommended by Indianapolis Monthly, FOX59, Wish-tv 8

  30. Worth the detour · Breweries, Bars & Cocktails · Downtown & Wholesale District

    Taxman CityWay

    Order: Belgian-style frites and Liège waffles with Taxman's Belgian-style house beers. Taxman Brewing's downtown gastropub and beer garden in an 1800s livery building in CityWay — Indiana-beef burgers, Belgian frites, 20 house drafts.

    Look for CityWay

    310 S Delaware St (CityWay), Indianapolis, IN

    Recommended by Indianapolis Monthly, Indianapolis Business Journal, Visit Indy

  31. Worth the detour · Pizza & Italian · Downtown & Wholesale District

    Iozzo's Garden of Italy

    Order: Family-recipe red-sauce Italian (meatballs, lasagna) from a 1930 lineage. Revival (2009) of Indianapolis's first full-service Italian restaurant, opened by Santora 'Fred' Iozzo in 1930 — his great-granddaughter cooks the family recipes in a near-south-side room by Lucas Oil Stadium.

    946 S Meridian St, Indianapolis, IN

    Recommended by Indianapolis Monthly, Wish-tv 8, FOX59

  32. Worth the detour · American & New American · Downtown & Wholesale District

    The Hulman

    Order: House pastas (short-rib spaccatelli); tableside king-crab bisque. Hotel Indy's 52-seat restaurant named for the Hulman family of the Speedway — chef Patrick Russ (ex-Next, Chicago) makes the pastas and sausages in house; Indianapolis Monthly 3 stars.

    Hotel Indy, 141 E Washington St, Indianapolis, IN

    Recommended by Indianapolis Monthly, Wish-tv 8, Indianapolis Business Journal

  33. Worth the detour · Downtown & Wholesale District

    Indiana State Museum

    The state's history-and-science museum on the canal in White River State Park, with an IMAX theatre and a sculpture in every Indiana county's limestone on the façade.

    650 W Washington St, Indianapolis, IN 46204

    Recommended by Downtown Indy, Inc., Wikipedia

  34. Worth the detour · Downtown & Wholesale District

    Indianapolis Union Station

    The 1888 Romanesque Revival head-house of the world's first union station, with its barrel-vaulted Grand Hall and rose window.

    39 Jackson Place, Indianapolis, IN

    Recommended by Wikipedia, National Park SVC

  35. Worth the detour · Downtown & Wholesale District

    Gainbridge Fieldhouse

    The Pacers' and Fever's retro-styled 1999 fieldhouse, built to evoke Indiana high-school gyms.

    125 S Pennsylvania St, Indianapolis, IN

    Recommended by Wikipedia, Indyencyclopedia

  36. Deep cut · Soul, BBQ & Southern · Downtown & Wholesale District

    Doc Crow's Southern Smokehouse and Raw Bar

    Order: House-rubbed smokehouse barbecue, raw-bar oysters, 750+ bourbons. Louisville's 16-year-old smokehouse-and-raw-bar opened its first Indiana outpost (May 2025) in the Hyatt Place across from Gainbridge Fieldhouse, in the old Pier 48 space — dry-rubbed barbecue and one of downtown's deepest bourbon walls.

    Look for Wholesale District

    130 S Pennsylvania St (Hyatt Place), Indianapolis, IN

    Recommended by Indianapolis Monthly, Wish-tv 8, FOX59, Indianapolis Business Journal

  37. Deep cut · Breweries, Bars & Cocktails · Downtown & Wholesale District

    Cannon Ball Rooftop Lounge

    Order: Indy-inspired cocktails and Midwest bites on an open-air rooftop. Sixth-floor open-air rooftop bar at Hotel Indy named for racer Erwin 'Cannon Ball' Baker — a slight Art Deco feel and some of the best downtown skyline views.

    Hotel Indy (6th floor), 141 E Washington St, Indianapolis, IN

    Recommended by Visit Indy, Axios Indianapolis, Indianapolis Monthly

Mass Ave, Lockerbie & the Old Northside 20

  1. Must see · Mass Ave, Lockerbie & the Old Northside

    Landmark for Peace Memorial

    Where Robert F. Kennedy broke the news of Martin Luther King Jr.'s assassination to a crowd on April 4, 1968 — Greg Perry's 1994 sculpture shows the two men reaching toward each other. Dedicated by President Clinton in 1995.

    Dr. Martin Luther King Jr. Park, 1702 N Broadway St, Indianapolis, IN

    Recommended by Wikipedia, Arts Council of Indianapolis (Indy Arts Guide), Indyencyclopedia, Visit Indy

  2. Must see · Mass Ave, Lockerbie & the Old Northside

    Mass Ave Cultural Arts District

    One of the four diagonal avenues of the 1821 plan: theatres, galleries, bars and the Mass Ave commercial historic district (NRHP 1982) — the city's main walking-and-eating strip.

    Look for Mass Ave

    Massachusetts Ave, Delaware St to I-65, Indianapolis, IN

    Recommended by Wikipedia, National Park SVC, Indyencyclopedia, The Cultural Landscape Foundation

  3. Must see · American & New American · Mass Ave, Lockerbie & the Old Northside

    Tinker Street

    Order: Seasonal small plates and the wine list in a 16th Street urban cottage. Tom Main's restaurant and wine bar between Herron-Morton Place and the Old Northside; Main was a James Beard Outstanding Restaurateur semifinalist (2025, 2026). An Indianapolis Monthly Best Restaurant.

    Look for Old Northside

    402 E 16th St, Indianapolis, IN 46202

    Recommended by James Beard, Indianapolis Monthly, Wish-tv 8, Visit Indy

  4. Must see · Steakhouses & Fine Dining · Mass Ave, Lockerbie & the Old Northside

    Vida

    Order: The chef's tasting menu with wine pairings. Lockerbie Square fine dining — the city's only AAA Four Diamond restaurant per WRTV. James Beard semifinalists: chef Thomas Melvin (Best Chef: Great Lakes, 2022) and GM/wine director Jared May (beverage/bar service, 2025 & 2026).

    Look for Lockerbie

    601 E New York St, Indianapolis, IN

    Recommended by James Beard, Indianapolis Monthly, WRTV 6 (abc Indianapolis), Downtown Indy, Inc.

  5. Must see · Soul, BBQ & Southern · Mass Ave, Lockerbie & the Old Northside

    Kountry Kitchen Soul Food Place

    Order: Fried chicken, smothered pork chops, greens and mac and cheese. Near-northside soul food landmark — Barack Obama lunched here on the 2008 campaign and Shaquille O'Neal called it the best soul food ever. Rebuilt on its original site after a 2020 fire, with the 910 North event hall.

    1831 N College Ave, Indianapolis, IN

    Recommended by Indianapolis Business Journal, FOX59, Wish-tv 8, Indianapolis Monthly

  6. Must see · Delis, Sandwiches & Diners · Mass Ave, Lockerbie & the Old Northside

    Goose the Market

    Order: The Batali — Smoking Goose coppa, soppressata and capocollo with provolone and giardiniera. Chris Eley's butcher-and-charcuterie market in Herron-Morton Place, birthplace of Smoking Goose Meatery (2011); its Batali sandwich is one of Indianapolis Monthly's 25 Essential Eats and Bon Appétit ranked it among the top ten sandwich shops in the US.

    Look for Herron-Morton Place

    2503 N Delaware St, Indianapolis, IN 46205

    Recommended by Indianapolis Monthly, Current, Nuvo, Visit Indy

  7. Must see · Pizza & Italian · Mass Ave, Lockerbie & the Old Northside

    Bazbeaux Pizza

    Order: Quattro Formaggi pie; thin crust with pine nuts, prosciutto and a mozzarella–provolone–pecorino blend. Indy's pizza institution since 1986 (Broad Ripple), on Mass Ave since 1989 — 'consistently local pizza lovers' favorite', with a string of Best of Indy titles; named Indiana's best family pizza joint.

    329 Massachusetts Ave, Indianapolis, IN

    Recommended by Indianapolis Monthly, Indianapolis Business Journal, Wish-tv 8, FOX59

  8. Must see · Mass Ave, Lockerbie & the Old Northside

    The Athenaeum (Das Deutsche Haus)

    The 1893-98 Vonnegut & Bohn German-American clubhouse — the most ornate building of German Indianapolis, still home to the Rathskeller (1894) and its biergarten.

    Look for Lockerbie

    401 E Michigan St, Indianapolis, IN

    Recommended by Wikipedia, Indyencyclopedia, Indiana Historical Society

  9. Must see · Mass Ave, Lockerbie & the Old Northside

    Benjamin Harrison Presidential Site

    The 23rd president's 16-room 1875 Italianate home (NHL 1964) — he ran the 1888 Front Porch Campaign from its porch and died upstairs in 1901. Guided tours.

    Look for Old Northside

    1230 N Delaware St, Indianapolis, IN 46202

    Recommended by Wikipedia, National Park SVC, Indyencyclopedia

  10. Must see · Mass Ave, Lockerbie & the Old Northside

    James Whitcomb Riley Museum Home

    The 1872 Lockerbie Square house where the 'Hoosier Poet' lived as a paying guest from 1893 until 1916 — preserved as he left it (NHL 1962), on the cobbled heart of Indy's oldest neighbourhood.

    Look for Lockerbie

    528 Lockerbie St, Indianapolis, IN

    Recommended by Wikipedia, Indyencyclopedia, Saharchipedia

  11. Must see · Mass Ave, Lockerbie & the Old Northside

    Monon Trail (10th Street trailhead)

    The 28.5-mile rail-trail on the old Monon Railroad, from 10th Street up through Broad Ripple and Carmel to Sheridan — Indy's busiest trail and the spine of the north side.

    Monon Trail at E 10th St, Indianapolis, IN

    Recommended by Wikipedia, TrailLink (Rails-to-Trails Conservancy), Backpacker magazine

  12. Must see · Breweries, Bars & Cocktails · Mass Ave, Lockerbie & the Old Northside

    The Rathskeller

    Order: Schnitzel, sauerbraten, ochsenschwanz suppe; the biergarten in summer. Indianapolis' oldest restaurant still operating (1894), in the cellar and biergarten of the Athenaeum — German food and a Kellerbar beer list.

    Look for Lockerbie

    401 E Michigan St, Indianapolis, IN

    Recommended by Visit Indy, The Takeout, Wikipedia

  13. Must see · Coffee & Cafés · Mass Ave, Lockerbie & the Old Northside

    Coat Check Coffee

    Order: Pistachio latte (house pistachio orgeat, rose water, lemon peel); currywurst croissant. Three-level café in the Athenaeum's old coat-check rooms — grand staircase, stained glass, German-leaning pastries; its pistachio latte is a cult order among Indy coffee people.

    Look for Lockerbie

    401 E Michigan St (The Athenaeum), Indianapolis, IN

    Recommended by Indianapolis Monthly, Axios Indianapolis

  14. Worth the detour · Mass Ave, Lockerbie & the Old Northside

    Bottleworks District & The Garage Food Hall

    The 1931 Art Deco Coca-Cola bottling plant reborn (2018-) as a hotel, cinema and The Garage food hall with ~18 vendors.

    Look for Mass Ave

    Bottleworks District (Mass Ave & College Ave), Indianapolis, IN

    Recommended by Wikipedia, Indyencyclopedia, WFYI, Time Out

  15. Worth the detour · American & New American · Mass Ave, Lockerbie & the Old Northside

    Bru Burger Bar

    Order: Three-meat (sirloin, chuck, brisket) burger; the Bru Burger with taleggio and tomato jam. Mass Ave burger bar from Cunningham Restaurant Group — Reader's Digest named it Indiana's best burger; Indianapolis Monthly Best of Indy No. 9.

    410 Massachusetts Ave, Indianapolis, IN

    Recommended by Indianapolis Monthly, FOX59, Indianapolis Business Journal, Wish-tv 8

  16. Worth the detour · Mass Ave, Lockerbie & the Old Northside

    Morris-Butler House

    D.A. Bohlen's c.1864 Second Empire mansion in the Old Northside, restored by Indiana Landmarks as a Victorian house museum.

    Look for Old Northside

    1204 N Park Ave, Indianapolis, IN

    Recommended by Wikipedia, Indyencyclopedia, Official Site

  17. Worth the detour · Mass Ave, Lockerbie & the Old Northside

    Old National Centre (Murat Shrine)

    The 1909 Murat Shrine temple, a Moorish-Revival fantasy of minarets and terra cotta — the oldest stage house in Indianapolis, now a concert venue.

    Look for Mass Ave

    502 N New Jersey St, Indianapolis, IN

    Recommended by Wikipedia, Indyencyclopedia, Saharchipedia

  18. Worth the detour · Mass Ave, Lockerbie & the Old Northside

    Indiana Landmarks Center

    The 1891 Romanesque Central Avenue Methodist Church, rescued and reopened in 2011 as the headquarters of Indiana Landmarks — the Cook Theater sanctuary keeps its stained glass.

    Look for Old Northside

    1201 Central Ave, Indianapolis, IN 46202

    Recommended by Indyencyclopedia, Indiana Public Media, Official Site

  19. Worth the detour · Mexican & Latin · Mass Ave, Lockerbie & the Old Northside

    Bakersfield Mass Ave

    Order: Achiote-braised pork tacos; 100 tequilas and bourbons. Late-night taco-tequila-whiskey bar of timbers, barrels and Edison bulbs — on Indianapolis Monthly's 25 Best Tacos list.

    334 Massachusetts Ave, Indianapolis, IN

    Recommended by Indianapolis Monthly, Wish-tv 8, Visit Indy

  20. Worth the detour · Breweries, Bars & Cocktails · Mass Ave, Lockerbie & the Old Northside

    St. Joseph Brewery & Public House

    Order: Confessional IPA brewed where the pulpit stood. Brewpub inside a 135-year-old former Catholic church — a bar built from old pews and floor joists, the brewhouse where the altar was, award-winning Confessional IPA.

    Look for St. Joseph

    540 N College Ave, Indianapolis, IN

    Recommended by Indianapolis Monthly, Wish-tv 8, Visit Indy

Fountain Square, Fletcher Place & the near south 14

  1. Must see · American & New American · Fountain Square, Fletcher Place & the near south

    Bluebeard

    Order: The daily-changing New American menu with bread from sister bakery Amelia's. Fletcher Place gastropub in a 1924 warehouse, named for Kurt Vonnegut's 12th novel; Indy's most James Beard-recognised restaurant (Abbi Merriss, Best Chef: Great Lakes semifinalist 2023). Now led by chef Alan Sternberg.

    Look for Fletcher Place

    653 Virginia Ave, Indianapolis, IN

    Recommended by James Beard, Indianapolis Monthly, Indianapolis Business Journal, Wikipedia

  2. Must see · Fountain Square, Fletcher Place & the near south

    Fountain Square Theatre Building

    1928 theatre block anchoring Fountain Square — a hotel, rooftop, and the Midwest's only duckpin bowling (Atomic Bowl's 1950s lanes, Action Duckpin's 1930s ones).

    Look for Fountain Square

    Fountain Square Theatre Building, Shelby St at Virginia Ave, Fountain Square, Indianapolis, IN

    Recommended by Wikipedia, National Park SVC, Roadside America

  3. Must see · Mexican & Latin · Fountain Square, Fletcher Place & the near south

    La Margarita

    Order: Tacos and margaritas. Fountain Square's beloved family Mexican spot, which closed unexpectedly in early 2025 and rose again in July 2025 on Virginia Ave in Fletcher Place (ground floor of the Slate apartments).

    Look for Fletcher Place

    501 Virginia Ave, Indianapolis, IN

    Recommended by Axios Indianapolis, Indianapolis Monthly, Indianapolis Business Journal

  4. Worth the detour · Fountain Square, Fletcher Place & the near south

    Holy Rosary Church & Italian Street Festival

    The 1909 church of Indy's Sicilian and Calabrian immigrants; its Italian Street Festival (since 1934) draws ~40,000 people each June for 25+ Italian dishes and a procession.

    520 Stevens St, Indianapolis, IN

    Recommended by Indyencyclopedia, WRTV 6 (abc Indianapolis), Wish-tv 8, Clio (Marshall University)

  5. Worth the detour · American & New American · Fountain Square, Fletcher Place & the near south

    Kuma's Corner

    Order: Metal-band-named burgers and craft beer. Chicago's heavy-metal burger bar on the corner of Morris and Prospect — its first location outside Chicago; reopened after a fire.

    1127 Prospect St, Indianapolis, IN

    Recommended by Indianapolis Monthly, Indianapolis Business Journal, Wish-tv 8, WRTV 6 (abc Indianapolis)

  6. Worth the detour · American & New American · Fountain Square, Fletcher Place & the near south

    Easy Rider Diner

    Order: Southwest-leaning brunch plates and vegan brunch options. Scruffy rock-star diner from Hi-Fi/MOKB's Josh Baker in the historic G.C. Murphy Building, next to the Hi-Fi music venue — morning-to-night brunch with Southwestern flavours.

    1043 Virginia Ave, Indianapolis, IN

    Recommended by Indianapolis Monthly, Axios Indianapolis, WTHR 13, Indianapolis Business Journal

  7. Worth the detour · Breweries, Bars & Cocktails · Fountain Square, Fletcher Place & the near south

    Metazoa Brewing Co.

    Dog-friendly brewery with its own dog park off South College Ave that gives 5% of profits to animal and wildlife groups; its Hoppopotamus IPA is on taps all over town. Indianapolis Monthly Best New Breweries.

    Look for Fletcher Place

    140 S College Ave, Indianapolis, IN

    Recommended by Indianapolis Monthly, Axios Indianapolis, Downtown Indy, Inc.

  8. Worth the detour · Breweries, Bars & Cocktails · Fountain Square, Fletcher Place & the near south

    Hotel Tango Distillery

    Order: Its own house-distilled spirits, poured in tasting-room cocktails. Fletcher Place micro-distillery — the first service-disabled, combat-veteran-owned artisan distillery in the US — with a tasting room pouring its own spirits; one of the openings that turned Fletcher Place into a food-and-drink district.

    Look for Fletcher Place

    702 Virginia Ave, Indianapolis, IN 46203

    Recommended by Indianapolis Monthly, Indianapolis Business Journal, Visit Indy

  9. Worth the detour · Asian · Fountain Square, Fletcher Place & the near south

    Siam Square

    Order: Thai curries and noodle dishes. Ed Rudisell's locally owned Thai restaurant in historic Fountain Square, long rated one of Indy's best ethnic restaurants.

    936 Virginia Ave, Indianapolis, IN

    Recommended by Indianapolis Monthly, Indianapolis Business Journal, Visit Indy

  10. Worth the detour · American & New American · Fountain Square, Fletcher Place & the near south

    Dugout Bar

    Order: Fried bologna sandwich and cheap domestics. Fletcher Place's 1954 neighbourhood bar on Virginia Ave's restaurant row — where the chefs and servers drink after their shifts; named Indiana's best dive bar.

    621 Virginia Ave, Indianapolis, IN 46203

    Recommended by WRTV 6 (abc Indianapolis), Indianapolis Monthly, Indy Today (6AM City)

  11. Worth the detour · Fountain Square, Fletcher Place & the near south

    Fletcher Place Historic District

  1. Must see · Midtown

    1870s Second Empire courthouse and sheriff's residence/jail (NRHP) at the centre of Noblesville's historic square — where Klan Grand Dragon D.C. Stephenson was convicted of murder in 1925, breaking the Indiana Klan.

    Look for Noblesville

    Courthouse Square (Logan, 8th, 9th & Conner Sts), Noblesville, IN

    Recommended by Wikipedia, National Park SVC, Indyencyclopedia

  3. Must see · American & New American · North suburbs

    Order: Samir Mohammad's globally inspired small menu. Tiny Noblesville bistro opened 2021 by Samir and Rachel Mohammad; Samir was a James Beard Best Chef: Great Lakes semifinalist (2023). On Indianapolis Monthly's Best Restaurants 2025 and 2026.

    Look for Noblesville

    56 S 9th St, Noblesville, IN

    Recommended by James Beard, Indianapolis Monthly, Current

  4. Must see · Breweries, Bars & Cocktails · North suburbs

    Order: Crispy lamb ribs with chimichurri; maple-bacon Brussels sprouts; house beers. Westfield's chef-driven brewpub (2018) — ex-Cerulean/Bluebeard chef Alan Sternberg, twice a James Beard Rising Chef nominee, runs the kitchen beside the Dikos family's house brews. Indianapolis Monthly Best Restaurants 2026.

    Look for Westfield

    303 E Main St, Westfield, IN

    Recommended by Indianapolis Monthly, Current, Townepost

  5. Must see · Steakhouses & Fine Dining · North suburbs

    Anthony's Chophouse

    Order: Single-sourced Greeley, Colorado corn-fed steaks; the original Glass Chimney bar. Glass-walled 9,000 sq ft Carmel steakhouse from the Ritz Charles family, white tablecloths and green velvet, with the bar salvaged from the beloved Glass Chimney. Indianapolis Monthly Best New Restaurants 2019; 'Face of Steaks' 2025.

    201 W Main St, Carmel, IN

    Recommended by Indianapolis Monthly, Current, Visit Hamilton County

  7. Worth the detour · North suburbs

  11. Worth the detour · North suburbs

South side 13

Greenwood, Beech Grove, Southport — 'Chindianapolis'

  1. Must see · South side

    Garfield Park & Conservatory

    Indianapolis' oldest city park (128 acres, NRHP) — George Kessler's 1916 Sunken Garden with fountains, and the 1954 aluminium-framed conservatory, the first of its kind in the US.

70 sights and 86 places to eat across Indianapolis — downtown and Monument Circle, Mass Ave, Fountain Square, Broad Ripple, Irvington, the Speedway — plus the north suburbs and the south side. Each is traceable to the source that named it. Indy’s canon is its own: the breaded pork tenderloin sandwich, sugar cream pie, St. Elmo’s fiery shrimp cocktail, Shapiro’s deli, fried biscuits & apple butter, the Burmese/Chin kitchens of the south side and the International Marketplace’s global corridor.

How this guide was made

How the cuisine filters were policed

Every food card names a specific dish — a cuisine label alone doesn’t qualify. Indianapolis’s canon is its own: the breaded pork tenderloin sandwich, sugar cream pie (the Hoosier pie), St. Elmo’s horseradish-fired shrimp cocktail, Shapiro’s deli, persimmon pudding, fried biscuits & apple butter, the Burmese & Chin kitchens of the south side and the International Marketplace’s global corridor, sourced to IndyStar, Indianapolis Monthly and the IBJ. A cuisine tag names the kitchen’s own tradition, never one dish it happens to serve.

Web-searched and fact-checked

Every place is traceable to a credible source — IndyStar, Indianapolis Monthly, the Indianapolis Business Journal, WFYI, Mirror Indy, Visit Indy, James Beard, NPS, Indiana DNR, Atlas Obscura and official sites — recorded in data/sources.json. Every coordinate is verified into data/geocodes.json and every place status-checked. Yelp/TripAdvisor never count toward the two-source bar.
